note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Is heat rejected to cooling water in one place while steam heats a colder stream in another (a heat-integration question)?

evidence.text: instrument FT-A reads "FT-A COOLING WATER supply candidate" at U-A
valve FV-B reads "FV-B STEAM heating supply candidate" at U-B

data_requests.item: Temperatures and duties of the cooled and the heated streams
where: historian or DCS trend for FT-A (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)
only a valve (FV-B) is drawn on this line, with no flow measurement; flow needs a meter or a calibrated valve curve
site records: heat and material balance
data_requests.how: For each stream: supply and target temperature and duty.

data_requests.item: Whether the duties overlap in time
where: site records: operating sequence: are both duties needed at the same time?
data_requests.how: Mark each duty continuous, batch or startup-only.

where: a walkdown: distance between the two exchangers
data_requests.how: Note pipe run and fouling service.

questions.decision_rule: Worth a pinch or exchanger study only when the hot stream's temperature range sits above the cold stream's with a practical approach, both run at the same time for long hours, and they are close enough to connect. Otherwise close this screening investigation.

typical_benefit.wording: Pinch potential "far exceeds that from well-known conventional techniques such as heat recovery from boiler flue gas, insulation and steam trap management." No % stated in that section.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.243x; 2.244x (IAC/ITAC browse page: 2.243x: 3,673 recommendations, 1.4 yr average payback, 31.2% implemented; 2.244x: 1,466 recommendations, 1.7 yr, 28.6%; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S19: Worrell & Galitsky, Energy Efficiency Improvement and Cost Saving Opportunities for Petroleum Refineries: An ENERGY STAR Guide (LBNL-56183, Feb 2005)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: A screen pairs any cooling-water-cooled item with any steam-heated item; the temperatures decide. On a reactive system any heat-integration change needs a hazard review first. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers.
